expectations.text: Each criterion is a design property — something an internal reviewer can score from the artifact itself, not a downstream user outcome that requires post-ship measurement, not a business metric
expectations.evidence: Criterion 6 'Distinct from agenda templates, HR software, and notebooks' and criterion 7 'Coherent strategic bet' are meta-properties about the direction's positioning/thesis rather than design properties scoreable from the artifact. Criterion 8 'Reviewable as a design, not just as an idea' is a meta-criterion about specificity, not a design property.

expectations.text: Each property has a named failure-mode-of-overpursuit — the trade-off is explicit: 'the failure mode to avoid is X'
expectations.evidence: Each of the 8 criteria has an explicit 'Failure mode of overpursuit' subsection naming what over-pursuit produces.

expectations.text: User-side outcomes translated to design-side properties — the brief's outcome is not restated verbatim with 'The design must' prepended; the design move that would produce the outcome is what's named
expectations.evidence: Each property names a specific design move (first-screen actionability, prompts that can be modified or ignored, on-screen differentiation by report type) rather than restating brief outcomes verbatim.

expectations.text: No business metrics including denumeralized ones — KPIs, conversion targets, retention rates, engagement metrics, growth metrics absent (and 'accelerate / increase / reduce X' patterns absent)
expectations.evidence: No KPIs, conversion, retention, or 'increase/reduce X' framings in the body of the criteria.

expectations.text: No regulatory constraints — regulatory frameworks are absent (those belong in design-constraints)
No craft-hygiene criteria — accessibility execution, design-system conformance, state completeness, semantic HTML, responsive CSS absent
expectations.evidence: No accessibility, design-system, semantic-HTML, or responsive CSS concerns appear as objectives.

expectations.text: No direction-specific criteria — every criterion applies to all viable directions for this brief, not to one specific candidate
expectations.evidence: Properties apply across viable directions; none presupposes a specific candidate. (Criterion 8 uses 'pre-1:1 briefing card with last-meeting notes' as an example of specificity, but as illustration, not as the criterion itself.)

expectations.text: Length appropriate — 4–6 short paragraphs, one per property
expectations.evidence: Doc has 8 numbered properties plus framing and 'how to use' coda — beyond the 4-6 paragraph range.
